12958.overview: This platform game has much in common with console games of the era. There are 4 worlds including ice, desert and fields, and have multiple routes through. The bad guys are cutesy. You get past them by spinning at them, although jumping over them is often sufficient. Power-ups on offer include speed ups, energy, food and water (Quik’s thirst and hunger are measured separately). The bonus levels involve jumping through time, by finding the right doors.

90989.overview:
So you want to be a hero? Then just pop into the Adventurer’s Guild, and study the notice board. There you will find offers of both honours and rewards, providing you are prepared to venture into the forest of Spielburg and risk all.

Played in the usual Sierra adventure-style mode, Hero’s Quest is classified as a Role Playing Game, but it has all the characteristics of an adventure as well as an RPG. 
Before commencing, a character must be set up. You’re offered a choice of Fighter, Magic User, and Thief as your personna.

The play progresses very much along the lines of a Sierra-style adventure, with just a little more emphasis on the acquisition of scrolls, potions, and weaponry. Until you meet up with something nasty in the forest, that is.
 
Fighting can be exhausting work, and you will need a few pieces of silver for a good night’s rest, not to mention the odd spell or two that you are short of! Make sure you never fail to search your victim’s body after his demise, for he may be carrying a fortune on his person!

Sound effects and music accompany many of the scenes and animated sequences. Most are a delight, and the animation is often quite humorous.
 
Because of the different character settings that can be achieved, together with random events, Hero’s Quest is unlikely to play the same way twice over. And fighting will take on a whole new dimension if you can throw a few nasty spells at your opponent rather than simply beating it to death!

Coming on five disks for the 1 Meg Amiga, Hero’s Quest is yet another high quality game from Sierra that is certain to give hours of fun and enjoyment.

121973.overview: As the second title in the Questron series, this game follows the same basic formula as the original. You start out as a lowly peasant with only a few gold coins in your pocket and a bad attitude to defend yourself. By stumbling around the countryside and fighting hordes of creatures, you gain wealth, experience, and title.

122800.overview:
Q-bic is loosely based upon the arcade classic. Fuzzball (AKA Q*Bert) and has been written by Ronald Weeserik. Ronald's no stranger to writing classic games on the Amiga and a few of his smashes are Silkworm, SWIV and Rodland.

The idea is to guide a blobby little sprite around a three dimensional pyramid by hopping from square to square and lighting up all the cubes in the structure. It all sounds very simple, but Ronald has included some devious nasties to compete with your sprite. Bubbles roll down the pyramid from top to bottom, whilst other similarly-shaped creatures may roll down and move from side to side.

Amazingly, Weeserik has chosen to release Q-bic onto the bulletin board circuit, and is not hoping to make any money out of the venture. Game is released as a Coverdisk on CU Amiga disk 41.

122831.overview:
The sequel to the first Quest for Glory game takes place in the town Shapeir and the desert surrounding it, in a Middle East-like environment. It seems that the powerful elemental spirits have been troubling the Shapeir folk recently. Something, or someone, is behind those troubles. It is your task to find out what is going on, to get acquainted with the many inhabitants of Shapeir and to prove once more you are worthy of your heroic title!

Just like its predecessor, 'Trial by Fire' is an adventure game with text-based interface, puzzles to solve, and characters to talk to, mixed with a role-playing character development system and battles. You can play as either a fighter, a thief, or a wizard, and also become a paladin in this game. The combat is action-based. You gain better parameters by fighting enemies, training, and performing other actions.

122833.overview: Quantox actually turned out to be rather good. The game is a dead simple shoot 'em up game with Jeff Minter overtones, but it's fast, smooth, slick and pretty, and it kept me entranced for ages. Lots of little bonus games stop it from getting repetitive, and even the power-ups have a touch of imagination about them. In fact, I'd go so far as to say that this is one of the most original blasters I've seen in a long time (in 1988). This has to represent, then, something of a major bargain.

125840.overview:
Qwak is a 2D platform/puzzle game developed by Jamie Woodhouse. It was initially released for the BBC Micro and Acorn Electron in 1989 as part of Superior/Acornsoft's Play It Again Sam 10 compilation. An updated and enhanced Amiga version was given a budget release by Team 17 in 1993. This update added several new features, including a two player mode and additional levels. The game was re-released on the Amiga CD32 later that year in a double-pack with science fiction shooter Alien Breed.

The object of the game is to guide a green duck through eighty levels. Fruit and gems can be collected for points, and enemies are eliminated with projectile egg weapons. Progress through the game is earned by collecting gold and silver keys. There are a variety of power-ups also available, including 'chocolate egg' weapons and extra shots.

In addition to the normal-style levels, the challenge levels require the player to complete levels and collect all fruit within twenty seconds.

Upon completion of all eighty levels, the levels are looped.

127273.overview: Quiksilver Pinball is an Amiga pinball arcade game released in 1990 by Actionworks

134558.overview: In this game, you guide a marker which must draw rectangles and other weird objects in order to claim your territory, and you can either draw these rectangles fast or slow. Drawing the rectangles using the "slow" method awards you the most points. Once a rectangle has been made, it will be colored in to show that you have claimed your territory. While drawing the rectangles, you need to watch out for Qix (pronounced "kicks"), a series of colored lines that crawl the screen. In addition to Qix, you also need to avoid the Sparks who travel around the border, as well as any lines that you have made, as well as The Fuse, who travels along the line that you are drawing. Once you have claimed enough territory, you proceed to the next level.

142269.overview: In Qatbol the player is in control over a one-screen level which represents a real-life wooden board. Just like a real board, the player can change its angle in all directions. The reason to do so is a little ball which is also on the board and its movement corresponds to the board movements. The player has to solve objectives which change from level to level, e.g. collecting things on the board or moving the ball into a hole. Of course there are also obstacles like teleports, holes or mazes.

142270.overview:
Quartz is a shoot 'em up with a variety of sections. The first section (and every odd-numbered one) is viewed from above and scrolls in every direction. As well as standard attack waves, there are large red/blue/yellow balls which split on impact a lá Asteroids, and once the smallest ones are destroyed they release tokens. Once you have collected 9 of each, you can choose a power-up form a range including various weapons, restart points (which effectively gives infinite continues when used with an emulator's 'snapshot' feature) and repairs to the ship. Destroying the whole of standard waves gives combined tokens which add one to each of the three colours.

The even-numbered waves scroll in a single direction, but include waves coming at you from other directions, even from within the screen in 3D. You can have up to 3 power-ups stored on your ship at a time, and choose one to activate by pressing F1-F3 - they all have limited firepower. Unusually, when you have no lives left, death results not in game over, but the loss of one of your power-ups (chosen by you).

142271.overview:
A long time ago, Lord Agravain roamed the land of Riva in his quest for the Elixir of Youth, the only hope for the all the ageing knights.

The Quest of Agravain is a platform game where the player controls a medieval knight armed with a sword. The main objective is to reach the exit door at the top of each level. Pressing the fire button makes Lord Agravain thrust his sword forward. Pressing fire while holding down makes him throw a weapon (the default one is a small lance). Like in Ghosts 'N Goblins, when the knight is hit he loses his armor. If he is attacked while semi-nude, he dies. There are several power-ups scattered throughout the 4 sets of levels (a cross paralyzes the enemies, a star gives invulnerability, etc). The game starts with three lives and has no form of saving progress.

143430.overview:
Based on the graphic novel of the same name, this computer game Quest for the Time-Bird is a marvellous saga whose principal ingredients are action, danger, suspense, fantasy and magic.

You have nine days to complete your quest by exploring this vast unknown world of wizards and spells with Roxanna, daughter of Mara the witch and Bragon, a retired knight who once again goes back into life of danger, all for the great Quest of the Time-Bird!

159728.overview:
Quadralien is a real-time puzzle game in the tradition of Sokoban.

The future: Mankind's space stations throughout the solar system are powered by a huge space reactor, called Astra. Astra is about to break down. The enemy race of Quadraliens has captured the reactor; now, contamination is rising and total failure is imminent. The last chance are six remotely controlled droids, which are to clean Astra and destroy the Quadrailen mother in Astras core.

You're controlling two robots in each of the 19 levels, cleaning up the contamination on your way. Gameplay is a variation of Sokoban: You've got to push spheres in the right direction to clear the way. However, the spheres are magnetically charged, meaning that they repell or attract each other. You've got to consider chain reactions. 

Before entering a level, you may chose which robots to take with you. Each droid has different abilities, like higher range of movement, higher capacity to carry contaminated materials, or a magnetic charge of its own. You can blast your way out of hopeless situations with a limited number of detonators, and you may restart every level with already removed contamination staying removed. However, there's a time limit for the whole game in form of reactor core temperature and energy, so be quick!

159730.overview:
Quadrel is a puzzle game in which you must fill each piece of the selected layout with different colored paints, without painting two adjacent pieces the same color.

At the beginning of a game, you can select the desired image or layout, as well as whether you wish to play with unlimited time or not. You can also select the "Imposed" game mode, in which the game points which piece you must fill next. Each layout has a set amount of paint available for use, in four different colors: red, green, blue and yellow. The amount of brush stokes left for each color is indicated on your palette. Some layouts have a large amount of a particular color and a very small amount of another, while other layouts have a more even amount of each color. The goal is to plan well from the start, so as to avoid running out of a particular color that will be needed to finish the layout.

The game can be played in solitaire mode, against the computer, or against another human player on the same screen. There are no sound effects during gameplay, only music. If you manage to finish a layout, you can enter your name in a high score table.

178217.overview:
An enemy with the codename ''Quake'', which is believed to come from another dimension, is using teleporter gates to invade Earth. The player takes the role of a nameless soldier who arrives at his base only to find out Quake has overrun it and killed everyone. Somewhere in the base there must be a teleporter to Quake's realm. The mission is clear: take the fight to the enemy, overcoming countless hordes of monsters, and exact revenge.

id Software's followup to Doom and Doom II, Quake is a first-person shooter. Its main technological innovation is the use of a true 3D engine - the levels themselves as well as the enemies are polygonal. This not only allows for more natural level designs and character animations, but also for more realistic lighting and the inclusion of simulated physics that have an effect on gameplay: grenades can bounce off walls and around corners, for example.

In single-player mode, gameplay consists mainly of proceeding through the levels (spread over four distinct episodes) in search of an exit, killing everything that moves. Interaction with the game world is reduced to a minimum: since there is no use key, buttons are pressed by running into or shooting at them. As in id's earlier games, many secrets are waiting to be discovered, including a few hidden levels.

Unlike Doom's rather straightforward design that couples futuristic environments with demonic imagery, the theme of Quake's levels, enemies and weapons is not so easily pinpointed. While each episode begins in a futuristic military base (with a technological 'slipgate' as the level exit), later levels take place in environments inspired by medieval fantasy and gothic horror (castles, dungeons and caverns) and the player passes through magical portals to advance. In a departure from Doom's colorful environments, all Quake levels are dominated by earth colors.

The enemies conform to the mishmash of designs: there are human opponents armed with shotguns and energy weapons in the early levels, while the later levels include medieval knights, ghosts, zombies, ogres (armed with grenade launchers and chainsaws) and some more unearthly beasts. The player's weapons, while relatively modern, all have a low-tech feel. Besides a (bloodstained) axe, there are shotguns, nailguns, rocket and grenade launchers and the Thunderbolt, which discharges electrical energy.

Quake was one of the first games playable natively over the Internet in addition to LANs. The single-player levels can be played cooperatively, but the game is most famous for its deathmatch mode. One-on-one duels, team play and free-for-all competition are possible. The emphasis is on fast reaction and skillful maneuvering through the levels. All of the single-player maps can be used as arenas, but the game also comes with six maps especially designed for deathmatch.

178219.overview: Quintette is a computer adaptation of the board game Pente. It also features Gomoku which is the game that Pente is a variant of. Both game modes are played on a board where two players place Go stones. The aim is to get five in a row or to capture five pair of the opponent's stones. The game can be played against an AI or against another human. It's also possible to watch a game with two AI players. Game options include using tournament rules or not and it's also possible to choose if black or white player should start or if there should be a flip for it. With tournament rules turned on the first player's second move is restricted and has to be at least three intersections away from the center of the board. The game features eight different difficulty levels. An option to modify the board is also included.

178220.overview:
Quiwi is a quiz game for multiple players taking turns. Players must answer questions from one of six different main topics like geography, art and literature or history and politics. After clicking the mouse once, an archer fires an arrow at a target that rotates colours corresponding to each of the main topics. The colour that is in the middle of the target once the arrow hits will be the topic for the next question. If the colour happens to be black, the player can directly select the topic of their choice.

Once a question has been asked, the player must first think about the answer and then reveal it by clicking on a button. If the player was correct, they can choose a "right" button, otherwise there are "wrong" and "no score" buttons. A right answer increases the player's score for the corresponding topic.

181437.overview:
QBall is a 1 - 2 player arcade 3-D billiards game for multiple systems.

The player plays billiards within a cube, where each corner represents the 8 separate pockets. The player aligns there shots with the white ball, and each player takes turns trying to place their shot. There is a 60 second shot clock, and the player can rotate the cube to examine the play area.

181438.overview: Quasar is a horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up where the player's task is to retrieve the stolen Eye of Quasar. To do so he has access to three star class five space ships that are equipped with ion shields that can absorb some damage before being destroyed. The default weapon of the craft is a pulse cannon but by collecting star mines it can be upgraded into, multi, laser and missile weapons. At the same time it's necessary to avoid tractor mines which can be deactivated by fire. The game consists of five different sectors that the player has to fly through. Many different obstacles will have to be navigated past, including meteor showers, sun corridors, underground caverns, acid seas and ice barriers. There will also be enemies in form of guardians which can only be destroyed by shooting at their power globes.

181439.overview:
This Codemasters Quattro compilation series contains the following four games:

SAS Combat Simulator
Kamikaze
Mig-29 Soviet Fighter
Guardian Angel (Freddy Hardest in South Manhattan)

205531.overview: Quasar Wars is a special kind of shoot 'em up because even if you will control a spaceship, here you will have complete freedom of movements (Thunder Force 1-like) unlike other games in which the scroll constantly "pushes" you to the right or to the top of the screen. To finish the game you will have to complete 16 missions spread over three worlds. But then again, not all of them will be the typical "kill them all" kind of missions you see in most shooters, since sometimes these will just be about recollecting certain number of capsules, or planting a bomb somewhere in the map. Of course, there will also be missions in which you have to kill everything that moves. Between missions, you can also select the items to equip on your spaceship or the weapons to use.

212817.overview: Move the three balls so they are in a row, all the while using blocks and balls to keep the monsters at bay. 20 levels of fun created by B Kraeuter and released in 1989.

212818.overview:
Quaptos is a timed puzzle board game. The goal of the game is to arrange an identical pattern in the second window within five minutes. Solving the task allows uncovering one part of prize picture. The screen is divided into three parts. Part one shows the information (points, remaining time, level code). Bottom window shows a pattern, which must be repeated in the upper window. Every square brick has a digit on it - initially "one". Each placed next to it brick increases the number by one point. After reaching the number "four" the brick number returns to "one". The bricks may be deleted at any time - in the reverse order of their placement on the board (last brick disappears first).

After each completed board the player receives a level code. The game allows to choose one of three available backgrounds.

212822.overview: A nicely done public domain soccer\football game created by G-Sfot and released in 1991.

214493.overview: Shoot your way through 5 increasingly difficult screens. Make blocks disappear by firing blocks at them. When they become cubes or cuboids they vanish. When you complete a stop block, the blocks will stop scrolling for 5 seconds. Tetris, mixed with a shooter and literally turned on it's head.

214494.overview: A charityware release, where the author desires you support a specific charity in order to own the game. The game is a breakout\Arkanoid clone whose author is Alexander Gebers and it was released in 1992.

214495.overview:
Quadrix is your perfect everyday "Finger Workout Game". Move QUADS around the board using the free cell. Try to get same color QUADS into winning shapes:

* 4 QUADS forming a square
* 6 QUADS in line (horizontal, vertical or diagonal)
* 4 QUADS on board corners

Try to achieve this quickly! If the time indicator reaches the end, some of your QUADS will get locked (you can't move them anymore). But don't worry! You can always form a winning shape with those QUADS and they will get unlocked. You are sometimes awarded BONUS QUADS:

* Time Freeze (freeze time for 30 seconds)
* Unlocker (unlocks QUADS colored like the current shape)
* X5 Bonus (the score for the current shape is multiplied by 5)

FEATURES
* Colorful graphics
* Fun sound effects
* Optional voice effects
* Background music
* Saves game state

This game is recommended for fans of puzzle games such as Trism or Bejewled.

Try to build your own strategy! Good luck!

214496.overview: Gather up the fruit for score and the keys to move to the next level, avoid the roaming baddies. When you get the proper keys the way out will open. Quackers is a freeware game created by Michael Pratt in 1990.

214497.overview: A single player puzzle game by Ben and Emma James that was released as shareware in 1993

214498.overview: In each screen, move the Quasimodo over the battlement of the castle to the upper right and ring the bell. Enemies will try to stab you and shoot projectiles at you that you must avoid. A PD game created by Paul Young and released in 1993.

214500.overview: Is a board game that can be played against the computer or another player. We won't reveal more here, except that it's great fun! Published as an Amigo! cover disk in August of 1995.

214501.overview: Quest for Galaxia is a video game for the Commodore Amiga platforms.  The game was released in 1993. The player controls a spaceship that can only move sideways.  The player is attacked by the opponent's spaceships that try to shoot him down.  The opponents come in clusters.  For each plane shot down, the player receives points. Published in Amiga Power 26 (Jun 1993)

214502.overview: A two-player only versus\duel game created by Ben Campbell and released in 1992 as an Amiga Format #35 (coverdisk 35b), June 1992. Game contains brief instructions on disk and supports PAL/NTSC screenmodes, mouse/joystick control plus a quit back to WB option. It is late within the 21st century. The public imagination is captured by network sponsored duels. Participants fight in arenas, remotely controlling their machines, matching their wits against each other and against preprogrammed droids. Fights are broadcast globally, there is much at stake.

214503.overview:
QX 2001 is a timed sci-fi arcade game. As a robot operator the player must find all parts of the indicated item (f.e. access card, transmitter) scattered around the base in order to get access to the next level. QX may shoot horizontally and vertically. The base is full of alien flying objects, turrets, laser barriers and robots. Contact with them means a loss of energy, which can't be supplemented.

The game features 3 levels.

216772.overview:
Quizam! is a 1 - 8 player trivia game for multiple systems.

Eight mysterious dark satellites orbiting the Earth must be destroyed. Their onboard computers have malfunctioned, generating an enormous volume of questions that are strange, cryptic- even trivial! Knowledge must be combined with careful strategy if you are to gain access to the satellites and succeed in this mission!

Players move about the board, trying to gather the eight satellites present on the screen. At the beginning of each turn, the player tries to correctly answer a 4-question multiple-choice question. The player receives movement points based upon how quickly they answer questions. The player must have the correct number of movement points to end their turn directly on top of the satellite. There are 8 different board layouts, 8 different difficulty levels, and games can be short or long.

418444.overview:
A sequel in name only, this follow up to id’s 1996 Quake, is a first-person shooter revolving around the Earth-Strogg war. The Strogg alien race threatens the Earth, but Earth has launched a counter-offensive, Operation Alien Overlord. Overlord takes the battle to the Strogg homeworld with the ultimate objective of securing their capital city and killing their ruler.

As a FPS, Quake II contains a variety of weapons including the fall back Blaster, the Railgun, and the secret BFG10K. Health, armor, and ammunition pick-ups can be found during levels, as can the classic Quake’s Quad Damage power-up. Game play involves mowing down alien opponents as the player progresses through levels, completing in-game objectives. Quake II also comes with multiplayer support for Deathmatches.

418584.overview:
When it comes to games of skill with a touch of tinkering, the simplest game ideas are usually the most ingenious - they say. man. But it is also said that every rule has its exceptions. Unfortunately, Silverbyte's dull "Kugelei" is such an exceptional case... 

The playing surface of Quattro consists of nothing but individual squares with different properties: some only allow the character (a small ball) to move horizontally, others only vertically; in later levels there are still dangerous killer fields. There are also malicious aliens, but also cute little barrels that give the lord of the ball extra life and extra time. Well, and what is the inclined player supposed to do with all that splendor? Nothing more than being in defiance of all the different special and special properties of the various fields. Maneuvering beads to the respective level exit under time pressure, as you might expect, it is of particular importance to plan your approach thoroughly before you send the marble on the long journey, otherwise you will quickly end up in a dead end.

421279.overview: A simple space invaders clone, each kill drops a green tokens that increase the score multiplier. Bonus enemies can also be killed for additional point bonuses. Boss levels to allow progress to the next wave.

422235.overview: Quasarius is a Galaga clone with a pleasantly fast framerate. Just like in Galaga, gameplay can be broken down into three phases: In the first one, you fight a number of enemies ships. In Quasarius, their formation changes slightly each level and there is only a single type of enemy ship. In the second phase, you fight a boss, a larger enemy ship. There is just a single boss type in Quasarius. Lastly, you fly through a danger zone, evading asteroids and other space debris while trying to pick up bonus points.

422260.overview: A single player adventure game by Ad Camp made in 1992. A mixed format game of text with multiple choices, pictures an overhead map of your surroundings and your score.

422263.overview: Take part in this multi-choice freeware, quiz game created by Graham Benham in 1992. The program also gives you the option of adding your own questions to the quiz. The categories are music, sport, television, news, film, pot luck, history, geography and people.

422273.overview: A shareware quiz game possibly based on questions from the Trivial Pursuit games or at least named after them. The game was released by A. Chetham in 1989.

422904.overview: A shareware game by Entactogenic Design, released in 1996. It was another normal day for Daisy, another day of eating grass when suddenly Daisy felt strange and looked at the mushrooms accusingly with rolling eyes. They got her jumping through the air. Sadly all this jumping led not only to Mad Cow Disease but to the first milkshake. Your local burger place is a ghost town and the government had to act quickly so they commissioned a robot, the Quicksilver to trace the roots of the craziness and eradicate it.

422905.overview: Die Quelle von Naroth is a shareware party-based role playing game. The mission is to fight an evil wizard which tries to weaken the land of Naroth by drain the land's most important water source. The game features a 3d view with step based movement and a tactical combat system. It's German language only.

423380.overview: A licenseware quiz game developed by Mat Fascione and published by Europress Software and Deja Vu Software in 1990 and re-released later in 1994. There were 4 versions of this game eventually released. Welcome to Quingo, a pub quiz machine simulator with 3000 questions in seven categories. These categories are geography, films, science and arture, people and more!

423388.overview: An unfinished platform game from Denice Software in 1989. Set in a fictional time when both humans and dinosaurs roamed the earth and attacked each other.

423430.overview: Quiz game for 1 - 4 people. Each player chooses a question from a field, after which four possible answers appear, which you can select with the joystick. With 300 questions/answers, HiScore list, score, time limit, risk, question editor to expand the question catalog and much more. Completely in German by author F. Zollner from 1989.

423431.overview: A German language quiz game released to public domain in 1988 by Critters.

423498.overview: A French language, shareware quiz game created by Alphatron in 1989. There was a limited demo version and the full version that included additional question sets.

423994.overview: A German language quiz program with over 700 questions from 12 different areas: general knowledge is required! Freeware game from Gerd Wagner from 1990.

449145.overview:
QUADRIGA is based on the timeless game idea of ​​getting four stones in a matrix into a straight line faster than your opponent. You might be able to beat your opponent, but can you beat the computer? 
 
Game is included on Amiga Spiele 1.

449147.overview: Available on POWER-DISC 6, this puzzle game was written in BASIC.

452042.overview: Gnosis or Q Game is a Greek-language freeware trivia quiz board game, similar to Trivial Pursuit from L-Soft (Lukas Konias) in 1993. A question editor has been included and the game can save high scores.

482653.overview:
Q*bert – Amiga version by TjLaZer 2026
Arcade original © 1982 D. Gottlieb & Co.
